# A module checked out under GOROOT/src, as a vendored submodule is, keeps
# its own module paths when a replace names its directory: listing that
# directory must not name it, or its imports, vendor/... as std would.

env GOROOT=$WORK/goroot
env GO111MODULE=on
env GOFLAGS=-mod=mod
cd $WORK/m

go list -f '{{.ImportPath}} {{.Imports}}' $GOROOT/src/vendor/example.com/sub/b
stdout '^example.com/sub/b \[example.com/sub/a\]$'

go list -f '{{.ImportPath}}' ../goroot/src/vendor/example.com/sub/a
stdout '^example.com/sub/a$'

# A directory of GOROOT/src that is no module's still takes its std path.
go list -f '{{.ImportPath}}' $GOROOT/src/fmt
stdout '^fmt$'

-- $WORK/m/go.mod --
module example.com/m

go 1.24

require example.com/sub v0.0.0

replace example.com/sub => ../goroot/src/vendor/example.com/sub
-- $WORK/m/m.go --
package m

import _ "example.com/sub/b"
-- $WORK/goroot/src/go.mod --
module std

go 1.24
-- $WORK/goroot/src/fmt/fmt.go --
package fmt
-- $WORK/goroot/src/cmd/README --
This directory must exist in order for the 'cmd' pattern to have something to
match against.
-- $WORK/goroot/src/vendor/example.com/sub/go.mod --
module example.com/sub

go 1.24
-- $WORK/goroot/src/vendor/example.com/sub/a/a.go --
package a
-- $WORK/goroot/src/vendor/example.com/sub/b/b.go --
package b

import _ "example.com/sub/a"
